title: Duke of Sessa to Charles V, Rome, 18 April 1524, RAH Salazar A-31 (9/31) ff. 128-131 (DECODE R9877-R9878)

documents.shelfmark: RAH Colección Salazar y Castro A-31 (9/31) ff. 128-131 (DECODE R9877, R9878 duplicate)

plaintext.source: No decipherment on the letter or its duplicate; Bergenroth's CSP Spain vol. 2 skips it. Sibling letters in the same cipher carry the court's decipherments (ff. 140, 172, 324).

transcription.source: DECODE images (R9877, R9878), cut into token tiles by tokens.py
transcription.notes: Nine cipher lines (eight on f. 128r, one on f. 128v); the duplicate ff. 130-131 is token-for-token the same. The transcription file mixes two passes and clear text, so it cannot be measured as it stands.

documents.shelfmark: RAH Colección Salazar y Castro A-31 (9/31) ff. 79-86 (DECODE R9873)

plaintext.source: No decipherment bound with it. CSP Spain ii 637 cites Goicoechea's 19th-c. deciphering (not imaged); no. 636 abstracts the triplicate's contemporary deciphering (Gayangos MS), no. 638 a court abstract. The English abstracts served as a topic crib only.

transcription.source: DECODE images in img/ (git-ignored), read in strips with a crop script
transcription.notes: Cipher runs on ff. 80v-84r and the postscript f. 86r; ff. 79r-80r, 84v-85v clear. Token count = the (a) lines of r9873_cipher.txt (--skip non-(a)/(c) lines --drop-first), so it includes f~ switches, v db openers and the few clear words quoted inside cipher lines. Read as sense (measure_read.py): 92.8% with pass-17 tentative values, 87.8% strict.

documents.shelfmark: RAH Colección Salazar y Castro A-34 (9/34) ff. 150-156 (DECODE R9898)

plaintext.source: Six cipher runs carry a contemporary marginal decipherment in a second hand (ff. 150r, 152r, 153v, 154r, 154v x3, 156r); the rest has none. Not calendared in CSP Spain iii.1.

transcription.source: DECODE images in img/ (git-ignored), read in strips with a crop script
transcription.notes: Clear and cipher interleaved throughout; heavy bleed-through on ff. 150v-151r and 155v. Token count as for r9873 (includes f~ and quoted clear words). Read as sense (measure_read.py): 79.8% with pass-17 tentative values, 77.9% strict.

documents.shelfmark: BNE MSS/20214/52-7 (Gayangos papers; Biblioteca Digital Hispánica, CC BY 4.0)

plaintext.source: No decipherment with it; not in CSP Spain ii (July 1524: nos. 661-663 only); DECODE R9893 (same day) and R9894 (29 Jul, CSP ii 663) are other letters.

transcription.notes: Brice Dudout's contribution (dudout/README.md). 1,340 code groups + 531 words in clear; the r-like sign split into three forms (A/B/C) after a pre-registered blind plate; read at 120 ppi by one reader.

system.summary: Mixed nomenclator: three-letter code groups for words, names and syllables plus single letters and signs for spelling, with a clear/cipher switch sign and a null paragraph opener.
system.sibling_key: Same cipher as Sessa's decrypted despatches of 1523-25 (ff. 138/140, 168-172, 322-324; R9897, R9893, R9834 and others); the key was rebuilt from them.
system.notes: About 110 code groups and the letter alphabet recovered (README). Homophones: several code variants (no ler/lex, con tat/tar). f~ switches clear/cipher; 'v db' is a null opener.

prior_solution.where: DECODE lists it Non-decrypted; not in CSP Spain; only sibling letters carry decipherments

conditions.human_role: Downloaded DECODE images logged in and supplied the DECODE cookie

solution.what: Identified DECODE's '1424' as 1524, the Duke of Sessa, Salazar A-31, and located the decrypted siblings in CSP Spain vol. 2.
Cut every cipher line of f. 128 and the siblings into token tiles; collated the duplicate f. 130.
Passes 1-9: aligned sibling ciphers (ff. 138, 168v, 170-171, 322) against their clears to assign code and letter values.
Passes 10-13: 1525 and July 1524 siblings (R9897, R9898, R9893) settled rad, lif, hud, zum and others.
Pass 14: template matching over the seven 1523 decrypted letters gave z y = -on; vo, per, ruc, hay remain unattested.
Word-level reading of the nine cipher lines, with four groups and one clause open.

Retry of the open groups (vo, per, ruc, hay, m-re clause) with the pass-15 key over the new full R9660 transcription; ruc gets five contexts (a verb/adjective root), none fixes a value; vo/per absent.
Took CSP Spain ii 636-638 (the 14 Apr 1524 despatch, its triplicate and the court abstract) from the BHO copy in targets/sanchez1523/csp; checked CSP iii.1 (BHO) for R9898: not calendared.
Transcribed every cipher run of R9873 (ff. 80v-86r) and R9898 (ff. 150r-156r) from the DECODE images in two-line strips into the (a)/(b) convention, appending page by page.
Found that R9898 is not without decipherment, as pass 12 had concluded: six cipher runs have a marginal decipherment in a second hand.
Aligned the six R9898 marginal decipherments: v em = cierto, li = mi, le = me, net = halla (not toma), lec = -mos, yol = aqui, sud = datario, Jac = obliga-, cap = tem-, nuh = grande.

Used CSP 636's English abstract as a topic crib for R9873: fed = rey de Francia (the pension; 'send a person under honest colour'), xir = cardenal, lot = nuncio, pof = exercito; values taken only where a second Spanish context agreed.

Cross-letter context: ruc/rus = dicho (pair of rad = dicha; 'el dicho datario', 'los dichos quatro mill ducados'), cuq = tengo, tig = contra, kuc = liga, yod/quf = amigo/enemigo, and the name Micer Agostino Foyeta; hay = aunque (tentative).
Read both letters with the pass-16 key; measured with measure_read.py (assembled words scored on es-golden-age): R9873 2165/2473 tokens (87.5%), R9898 2361/3059 (77.2%).
Retried the f. 128 residue with the new values: rus = dicho and hay = aunque give 'de lo susodicho, aunque no, me parece que concuerda'; vo and per occur in neither letter; the m-re clause unchanged.
About 260 code groups across the two letters (most attested once) and 398 letter tokens on the bleed-through pages of R9898 stay unread.

Pass 17: pooled the open groups of R9873, R9898 and R9660 into one concordance (84 groups in two or more letters) and took values that read in every occurrence (cas tiene, var agora, rac dize, pam/Jir paga, xoc socorr-, leg mucho, sur/luc parte, len/lon buen-, 3ar aca, yer Florencia, gig quisie-, nuf gente and ~15 single-context ones); all tentative.
Tested alphabetical bracketing of the code: attested values do not follow code order (cad sobre, cas tiene, cap tem-, cot todo), so no bracketing.
Re-cut R9873's non-word spellings and R9898 ff. 150v-151r at 1.5-1.6x: one correction (f. 83r p-u-e-r-e = pudiesse); the rest stand as written; bleed-through on R9898 does not resolve.
Looked for a better image of R9898 on the RAH Biblioteca Digital (search behind a bot wall; web search finds no digitised Salazar A-34).
Re-measured: R9873 92.8% (strict 87.8%), R9898 79.8% (strict 77.9%); the 95% target was not reached.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 3617 tokens, 206 types, es-golden-age order 4: reading -2.169 per letter; random keys -3.449 (z 6.3); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.421 (mean -2.434, z 34.3); annealer on the real text -2.167. Verdict: pass.

Full texts listed in outcome.texts (George Lasry's request of 22 Oct 2026): transcription_f128.txt with the reading copied from NOTES.md section 3 to texts/f128_decryption.md; r9873_cipher.txt and r9898_cipher.txt (cipher line with reading) with read_r9873.md / read_r9898.md; key key_working.md

Reading audit (George Lasry's sentence test, 22 Oct 2026): texts/f128_decryption.md, r9873_cipher.txt/read_r9873.md and r9898_cipher.txt/read_r9898.md read. f. 128's nine lines build Spanish sentences with single-word holes (reviewed B); R9873 and R9898 are line-by-line working files with an open group or non-word in most sentences and English gists, relabelled decoded, not read. fraction_read 0.9 (f. 128 only) -> 0.021 (tokens of all three documents in text that reads).

b23 re-read: DECODE records R9872-R9874, R9897-R9899 re-fetched logged in (research/reading_audit/b23_fetch.py). R9873's 8 images and R9898's 7 opened one by one: no attachment, comment, interlinear or slip decipherment beyond R9898's six known margins; R9874 = R9873 P6 + address leaf. R9899 (A-34 ff. 194-195, March 1525, same cipher) is a new sibling: its 13 cipher lines have no decipherment except one f. 194v run with a marginal one ('Su Sd. no querria estar de mejor animo y todos sus ministros van por el mesmo stilo'), giving hog = querria.

Quick web search for the Gayangos triplicate with contemporary deciphering (CSP Spain ii 636) and Goicoechea's decipherment of R9873 (CSP 637) in BNE Biblioteca Digital Hispanica and RAH Biblioteca Digital: neither found online. Lead noted, not followed: Kolosova's thesis El lenguaje secreto de la diplomacia de Carlos V (1521-1527) (Valencia; TESEO PDF; Salamanca 2024) describes 17 chancery ciphers of 1520-30 and names Sessa.

Open groups of R9873/R9898 pooled with R9899, f. 128 and R9660 (1523). Adopted where every occurrence reads: gal embia- (R9898 f.150r margin), hog querria (R9899 margin), kaz -mente (margin), reb dezi- (four contexts incl. R9660 contra-dezir-la), dis servido (servidores, servidor, sera servido), cer teni, lar miento, sur/luc parte, tt plural s, gul si, nuf gente, qu o, gom quatro with lo mill / ror ducado (the clear 'quatro mill ducados' then 'los dichos gom lo ror-s que se perdieron'); the sense-only ones flagged for review. Not adopted: all pass-17 values, hay (fails in f.81r), kam (two contexts disagree), yid favor (3 of 4 contexts), mjn (ha x8, Italia x3: two groups transcribed alike).

r9873_reading.md and r9898_reading.md built as continuous Spanish in the period spelling from the working decodes, open groups written [...grp], tentative values [?value], with word-level mends from the figures logged (ternia, atajar, demostracion, teniendose, no halla grand aliento, no se haze, ynposibilidad, veniesse, jamas huvo, ynresolucion, ynreparable, esas fronteras); every unbracketed word aligned with the decode or clear text (b23_sessa_align.py: R9873 0 uncarried of 1,534; R9898 0 apart from the date line carried by the section header). Look-alike letters: R9873 63 on 84 of 126 line pairs (3 as i 38), R9898 21 on 106 of 159. f. 83r ll. 19-24 re-checked on the image at 2x: transcription stands, no label changed.

Reading bodies scored: R9873 0.715 clean sentences counting explicit holes (b17_score HOLES=1), 0.399 plain, _check_reading 0.409 (working file before: 0.13); the sentences hold except f. 83r ll. 19-25: set read, grade B, English in r9873_en.md. R9898 0.47 HOLES=1, 0.273 plain (before 0.16): stays decoded, not read (bleed-through pages and some 140 single-context groups). fraction_read 0.021 -> 0.458 (f. 128 116 + R9873 2,473 of 5,648 cipher tokens).

Verify sweep (reading audit v2): R9873 reading re-scored with the sense-only values of the b23 log (sur/luc parte, tt plural s, reb dezi-, cer teni, lar miento, gom quatro, qu o, dis servido, gul si, nuf gente; 21 words located by their (a)-line contexts, research/reading_audit/v2_sessa1524_sense.py) and the unattested look-alike letters (v2_sessa1524_look.py: 29 letter cases outside 3 = i; the ꝍ-as-i/j/d, Є/ε-as-i/y and 3-as-j/l words, 11, counted; Ɉ u/v, ꝍ u/v, x r, ⅄, ∠, tto taken as declared second values) as holes. Explicit-hole share 0.632 (103/163), b17 HOLES=1 0.652; plain 0.38. Look-alike letters about 95 of roughly 7,900 reading letters (1.2%), most the attested 3 = i. Kept read.
Read bar applied per document (v10): 1 of 2 documents marked read measure under 95% of words read as sense (v2_score explicit holes) and are now read in part; read_share recorded for each.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.119; polyphony 0.053; 1936 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.167

texts.label: R9877 / R9878, Rome, 18 Apr 1524 (RAH Salazar A-31 ff. 128-131)
texts.summary: The Duke of Sessa, imperial ambassador in Rome, to Charles V (DECODE's '1424' is a typo): the bishop of Veroli's report from Constance on the Swiss diet and cantons arming for France; in cipher, that the Pope's secretary Felice would not show the bishop's own letters, that the report agrees with what the bishop wrote to the postmaster, and that Sessa asked the Pope for a provision for the Swiss business, having opened the peace-and-truce negotiation. Key rebuilt from the sibling letters' contemporary decipherments.

reading_review.note: texts/f128_decryption.md: the nine cipher lines build Spanish sentences (Felice would not show the bishop's letters; it agrees with what the bishop wrote to the postmaster; Sessa asked the Pope for a provision for the Swiss business, since he has the pretext, having opened the peace-and-truce talks) with single-group holes (vo, ruc/hay, pa) and one spelled clause unread; the sense is given in English. Audit grade C refined for f. 128: the holes are single words in a short passage whose frame holds.

texts.label: R9873, Rome, 14 Apr 1524 (RAH Salazar A-31 ff. 79-86)
texts.summary: Sessa to Charles V, a holograph with cipher runs and a postscript wholly in cipher; no decipherment is bound with it (Bergenroth's CSP Spain ii 637 calendars Goicoechea's 19th-century reading, and nos. 636/638 the triplicate and the court abstract, used only as a topic crib). Transcribed in full; each line (a) cipher, (b) reading.

reading_review.note: r9873_reading.md: the letter written out as continuous Spanish in its 1524 spelling from the working decode r9873_cipher.txt (key passes 1-17 plus the b23 values gal, hog, reb, dis, cer, lar, sur/luc, tt, gul, nuf, qu, gom/lo/ror, kaz; sense-only ones flagged in texts/r9873-r9898_reread_log.md), every word aligned with the decode or the clear text (research/reading_audit/b23_sessa_align.py: 0 uncarried). Clean sentences 0.715 counting explicit holes (b17_score HOLES=1), 0.399 plain (the es word list lacks the period spelling); holes are open code groups and tentative values. The sentences hold through ff. 80v-82v, 83v-84r and the postscript and agree topic by topic with CSP Spain ii 636; f. 83r ll. 19-25 does not hold. No contemporary decipherment of this copy is in reach (the triplicate and Goicoechea's reading are not imaged). Verified 23 Oct 2026 (reading audit v2): rescored with every word resting on a sense-only key value (sur/luc, tt, reb, cer, lar, gom, qu, dis, gul, nuf: 21 words) and every word carrying an unattested look-alike (ꝍ as i/j/d, Є/ε as i/y, 3 as j/l: 11 words) counted as a hole: 0.632 explicit holes (103/163, v2_score.py), 0.652 b17 HOLES=1, against 0.687/0.715 as published; 0.38 plain. Still at the bar; f. 83r ll. 19-25 remain the one passage that does not hold. Kept read, grade B.

texts.note: 24 Oct 2026: 88.3% of the words of r9873_reading.md read as sense (v2_score explicit holes); coherent sentences but under the 95% read bar, so read in part.

b23 re-read (23 Oct 2026): r9898_reading.md writes the letter out as continuous Spanish from the working decode, the six marginal decipherments followed where they stand, every unbracketed word aligned with the decode (b23_sessa_align.py). It scores 0.47 clean sentences counting explicit holes (0.273 plain), below the bar: the margin runs, the clear passages and ff. 151v-152r read, but the bleed-through pages (ff. 150v-151r, 155v) and most of ff. 152v-154r give spelled runs that make no word in nearly every sentence and some 140 code groups seen once. Pooling with R9873, R9899 (new sibling, one margin), f. 128 and R9660 closed none of them. Blockers: illegible (bleed-through; no gain at 1.5x/2x, DECODE's scans the only image) and no-key-material (single-context groups with no deciphered occurrence).
texts.label: R9898, Rome, 24 Feb 1525 (RAH Salazar A-34 ff. 150-156)
texts.summary: Sessa to Charles V, written on the day of Pavia, before the news: Italy, the Pope and the datary's attempt to bring the Duke over to the French; six runs carry a marginal decipherment of the time, the rest is read here with the key. Not calendared in CSP iii.1.

texts.label: BNE MSS/20214/52-7, Rome, 24 Jul 1524 (Brice Dudout)
texts.summary: Sessa reports the Pope's words: Italy confused since the viceroy left; the Pope pressed to join a league that England wants, which he has not and will not consent to; news by way of Bourbon; the French suspicious and fearful; the bishop of Bayeux now an avowed French ambassador; Casale to England; Alberto Pio back from Viterbo; the confirmation of the league; Pescara takes Saluzzo, the army unpaid. Key KS4 (your key + five BNE cipher/clear pairs and R9893) validated on the held-out pair 52-6; 630 of 670 cipher words read (94.0%).

reading_review.note: Read as sentences 4 Nov 2026 (Spanish 1524, read in part): views 000-001 read as continuous sentences (the Pope's message on the league, Bourbon, the French, the datary and the archbishop of Capua, Bayeux, Casale, Sigismondo, Alberto Pio, the confirmation of the league); view 002 holds except one run (V2gL04-05, 'para ‹gab›rse y ‹...› otros franceses'). 670 cipher words: 590 certain, 33 probable, 7 restored, 40 unresolved = 94.0%, so grade B and read in part. Key KS4 validated by one measurement on held-out BNE 52-6 (characters 0.860, words 0.772; 200 controls max 0.274/0.174).
